To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the receptor for organic CaCBs from rabbit lung is a member of the family of high voltage activated calcium channels.
the complete amino acid sequence has been deduced from the cDNA of the receptor for CaCB from rabbit lung and that the cDNA induces the functional expression of this CaCB receptor in Xenopus oocyte.
we have cloned the complete amino acid sequence encoding the CaCB receptor from rabbit lung.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular structure and the functional characterization of the receptor for CaCB.
the structure of the CaCB and the mechanism of its interaction with organic CaCB.
the primary structure, expression, and pharmacology of the receptor for the dihydropyridine CaCBs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the receptor for CaCB is a high voltage activated channel, which is expressed in a variety of tissues and which is encoded by the CaCB gene.
this channel is indeed the receptor for organic CaCBs.
the receptor for organic CaCB is a high voltage activated Ca2+ channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cDNA encoding the receptor for organic CaCB from rabbit lung was isolated, the amino acid sequence was deduced, the RNA was synthesized in vitro and the functional expression of the channel was induced in Xenopus oocyte.
we have isolated the cDNA for a high voltage activated CaCB‐sensing calcium channel from rabbit pulmonary artery.
the receptor for CaCB is a member of the family of voltage‐gated calcium channels and that the CaCB receptor is the first member of this family to be cloned and functionally expressed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a lot more diversity in the calcium channel family than previously thought, and that the receptor for calcium channel blockers is actually a calcium channel in itself.
the receptor for CaCB in the rabbit lung has the same primary structure as the CaCB receptor in the rabbit heart.
the CaCB receptor from rabbit lung is a member of a new family of calcium channels.
